title: Activity event
description: One thing a person did in their browser, as everything that reads the activity record sees it. read_events in seeress/activity.py makes an event from a line of the record, and Event.parse there reads one back. An event is a site, a path with no query and no fragment, a kind, a tab and a second. For a click, an input, a submit and a select it may also carry an action, which says what was done in the page and never what a field held. It carries no page title, no typed text, no query, no fragment and no full URL: what may reach a model is the site, the path, the hour and counts.

ts.description: The local time of the machine, to the second, as the logger writes it

site.description: A site: the host name, in lower case, without a leading 'www.' A browser accepts an underscore in a host name, as intranet servers often have one, and so does a site

path.description: The URL's path with its query and its fragment removed; '/' when the URL has no path

target.description: The tab, by the first eight characters of its identifier, or null when the logger cannot name it

action.description: What was done in the page, for a click, an input, a submit and a select, and for no other kind of event. A listener inside the page reports it, and that listener never reads what a field holds. An event that was not reported from inside a page has none

type.description: What was done. It is the event's kind

tag.description: The element's tag name, in lower case. A custom element's name always holds a hyphen, so a tag may

fingerprint.description: How the element is told apart on its page: its tag, and the first of data-testid, an id with no digit, a name and an aria-label that it has, with the digits of the others replaced by #. An element with none of the four is told apart by its place and the place of up to three parents. A value is cut at 200 characters

field.description: The kind of the field an input was typed into. It is there when type is input, and only then. A password, a one-time code and a card are named by their kind, and what was typed is never read
